sources: FRIDAY Oct 30 2026 RUN, pre-US-open (before 13:30 UTC). This run carries THURSDAY Oct 29 closes for VIX and Brent, FRED prints through Oct 28-29, and the first full read of the SEPTEMBER PCE and Q3 GDP released Thursday morning. HEADLINE: GROWTH CAME IN HOT AND INFLATION RE-ACCELERATED, WHICH VALIDATES WEDNESDAY TWO HAWKISH DISSENTS. DATA - THE BIG ONE. Q3 GDP first estimate plus 3.4 pct annualised against plus 3.1 pct expected, up from plus 2.2 pct in Q2. September PCE: HEADLINE 3.6 PCT Y/Y, UP FROM 3.4 PCT, plus 0.5 pct on the month; CORE 3.1 PCT Y/Y, UP FROM 3.0 PCT, plus 0.3 pct on the month. Real PCE slowed to 2.5 pct y/y from 2.7 pct and real disposable income to 1.0 pct from 1.3 pct. So the economy is running hot in nominal terms while real consumer purchasing power decelerates, and BOTH headline and core inflation are now rising, not fading. That is the single most important change on the board this week: for four runs the thesis was inflation-fading, and the September print kills it. The Fed statement language that inflation is STILL HIGH, and the Cook and Hammack dissents in favour of a 25bp HIKE, now read as informed rather than hawkish-for-its-own-sake. LABOUR - STILL FINE. Initial claims 194k for the week ending OCT 24, a NEW PRINT, down from a revised 195k; four-week average 196,750, down 1,250 from a revised 198,000. Continuing claims FELL to 1.701 million from a revised 1.722 million, reversing the six-week high that the last three runs flagged as the soft spot. Claims tile 194k, trend DOWN. There is no labour-market crack here. CURVE - THE FOMC STEEPENING HELD. FRED T10Y2Y Oct 29 at 0.37, giving back only 1bp of Wednesday 9bp jump to 0.38 (0.29 Oct 27, 0.32 Oct 26, 0.31 Oct 23). Against 0.31 a week ago that is plus 6bp, so the tile stays UP and the question the last run posed, whether the steepening was a one-day FOMC artifact, is ANSWERED NO. Yields eased on Thursday on the AI-driven equity selloff, but the SHAPE of the curve did not flatten back. BREAKEVEN - SECOND CONSECUTIVE RISE, AND NOW IT HAS A REASON. FRED T5YIFR Oct 28 at 2.27 pct, up 2bp from 2.25 and up 7bp from 2.20 a week ago, so the tile FLIPS FROM DOWN TO UP for the first time since the oil spike began. Two runs ago this series was making new lows. With September core PCE at 3.1 pct and rising, a rising 5y5y is the market doing exactly what it should. CREDIT - A NEW OCTOBER TIGHT, AGAIN. FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 Oct 28 at 3.14 pct, 4bp tighter than 3.18 and 24bp inside the Oct 22 month wide of 3.40 (3.38 Oct 23). Tile 318 to 314bp. Against 338bp a week ago that is minus 24bp, trend DOWN, and HY is at its TIGHTEST level of October. The Oct 22-23 credit scare is now fully erased and then some, for a third consecutive run. VOL - EQUITY VOL UP OFF THE MONTH LOW BUT STILL WELL DOWN ON THE WEEK. VIX 17.20 for the Oct 29 close, PLUS 1.71 pct from 16.91. Against 19.45 on Oct 23 that is MINUS 11.6 pct, so the tile is DOWN even though the day was up. The rise is an AI-earnings story, not a macro one: Alphabet fell about 12 pct, Microsoft guidance disappointed, the Nasdaq led the major indexes lower and the S&P 500 closed down about 0.30 pct, ending the three-session green run. Equity risk is being repriced inside the tech complex, not across the system. MOVE is CARRIED at 103.31 for Oct 23 for a FIFTEENTH consecutive blind run - Investing.com still stops at Oct 23 (106.84 Oct 22, 95.94 Oct 21, 101.70 Oct 20, 101.30 Oct 19). Against Oct 20 the carry reads plus 1.6 pct so the tile is held FLAT. THIS REMAINS THE BOARD WORST BLIND SPOT and it is blind in the week when a hot PCE and a held steepening are precisely what rate vol should be pricing. TREAT THE MOVE TILE AS BLIND, NOT AS CALM. OIL - THE SPIKE PREMIUM IS FULLY ROUND-TRIPPED. Brent 111.90 USD plus 0.99 pct this morning (TradingEconomics stats 111.89 for Oct 30, forecast table 111.95), after 114.10 on Oct 29 and a 115.32 close on Oct 28. Against 111.70 on Oct 23 (Investing.com futures close) that is plus 0.2 pct, so the tile moves from UP to FLAT. Brent is still plus 9.4 pct on the month, but the entire post-FOMC-week spike has now unwound on Iran diplomacy rather than on confirmed supply. THE SUPPLY RISK IS STILL LIVE AND STILL UNCONFIRMED: the Houthi claim on the 550,000 b/d Saudi refinery has gone unconfirmed by Riyadh for a TWELFTH CONSECUTIVE RUN. Interceptions keep being announced; damage never is. A confirmed hit is still the fastest way this board breaks. METALS - COPPER-GOLD MAKES ANOTHER NEW HIGH ON A GOLD SELLOFF. Gold 3,980.90 USD/t.oz MINUS 1.00 pct, BREAKING BELOW 4,000 for the first time in weeks (stats section 3,982.66 minus 0.96 pct); copper 6.5775 USD/Lbs, minus 1.03 pct. Copper-gold 6.5775/3980.90*1000 = 1.6523, tile 1.64 to 1.65, up from 1.57 a week ago. Trend UP, FIFTH consecutive run of improvement, and still the cleanest pro-growth signal on the board. Note the composition: this leg is gold falling faster than copper, i.e. the safety bid unwinding, which fits a hot-GDP, hawkish-Fed world. DOLLAR - FLAT, AND THAT IS THE ODD ONE. DXY 101.81 (TradingEconomics quote table 101.8129, ticker 101.808, minus 0.22 pct; stats section 101.8047 minus 0.06 pct), down from 102.14 last run. Against 101.79 a week ago that is plus 0.02 pct, so the tile stays FLAT. The FRED broad dollar index DTWEXBGS confirms a flat week (121.3202 Oct 23 against 121.3531 Oct 22, 121.3422 Oct 21). A hot GDP print, a re-accelerating core PCE and two hike dissents bought the dollar NOTHING in two sessions. That is a genuine inconsistency worth watching. FINANCIAL CONDITIONS - SAME PRINT, BETTER PRECISION, STILL EASY. FRED is now serving the NFCI week ending OCT 23 at MINUS 0.487 at three decimals, resolving the precision caveat the last run left open, against minus 0.494 the week before (minus 0.501 Oct 9, minus 0.508 Oct 2, minus 0.518 Sep 25). Tile minus 0.49, trend FLAT. Financial conditions have eased in a straight line for five straight weeks and the Oct 22-23 scare never touched them. Next update Nov 4. MACRO TILES - ONE NEW, ONE REVISED, THE REST CARRIED. Claims 194k is NEW (see above). Building permits REVISED to 1,398k SAAR for September from 1,400k, FRED page updated Oct 27; tile 1400 to 1398, trend FLAT, next print mid-November. Consumer sentiment 48.0, UMich October FINAL, confirmed against the September 48.1 and the October preliminary 46.3; the final was released Oct 23 so it was already in last week comparison base and the tile goes from UP to FLAT. Level is still a five-month low. LEI y/y CARRIED at plus 1.2 pct for September; the Oct 22 Conference Board release has the index UNCHANGED at 99.6 (2016=100), zero m/m, plus 0.6 pct over the six months March to September, and publishes NO y/y figure, so the 1.2 pct is carried from the prior run derivation and should be treated as low-precision. Trend FLAT, next release mid-November. ISM Manufacturing 54.5 September (54.6 August), next print MONDAY NOV 2. Sahm Rule 0.00 September, next Nov 6, trigger plus 0.50. GLOBAL LIQUIDITY - STILL 1 (STABLE), AND STILL ON THE OCT 21 SHEET. FRED WALCL has NOT yet posted the Oct 28 H.4.1 that was released Thursday; latest remains Oct 21 at 6,753,604 million USD, minus 2,035 million on the week (6,755,639 Oct 14, 6,747,560 Oct 7). No regime change at the ECB, PBOC or BOJ. Tile 1. Re-read WALCL next run. MONETARY PLUMBING - BLIND, FIFTEENTH RUN. The 3M SOFR-OIS spread is CARRIED AS A STANDING ASSUMPTION at 0bp, NOT a measurement. The EUR/USD 3M cross-currency basis is likewise a STANDING ASSUMPTION at minus 10bp. Every free source serves a SOFR level or an OIS rate but never the spread. Scorecard unchanged for a fifteenth run: two assumed tiles, one judgement tile (global liquidity), one stale tile (MOVE), one low-precision carry (LEI) out of eighteen. CALENDAR: OPEC+ SUNDAY NOV 1, expected to hold December targets. ISM Manufacturing MONDAY NOV 2. US MIDTERMS TUESDAY NOV 3. NFCI Nov 4. Sahm Nov 6. October CPI mid-November. Next FOMC December. INFRASTRUCTURE: git healthy before this run (HEAD 0f5b536, the Oct 29 commit); this scheduled session remains the SOLE writer of data.json; the GitHub Action stays disabled since Oct 17; BDTI stays removed since Oct 17. The .git lock-file pile keeps growing because this session cannot delete files in the folder - still harmless, but it WILL eventually break a git operation, and clearing it needs delete permission on the Dashboard Macro folder. STILL OPEN - SECURITY, FIFTEENTH RUN: the origin remote is an HTTPS URL with a GitHub personal access token in PLAIN TEXT in .git/config; it is fine-grained and repo-scoped, but it should be rotated and replaced with an SSH remote. Untracked junk still in the repo root: _stale_git_locks/, _wtest, __pycache__/ and outputs/. PICTURE: the board has gone from reflation-and-term-premium to CONFIRMED REFLATION. Growth is hot (GDP 3.4 pct), the labour market is fine (claims at a three-month low, continuing claims reversing), financial conditions are easy and easing, credit is at an October tight, equity vol is down on the week, copper-gold is at a new high, and the curve has held a 6bp weekly steepening. Against that, inflation is NO LONGER FADING: headline PCE 3.4 to 3.6 pct, core 3.0 to 3.1 pct, and the 5y5y breakeven has turned up two runs in a row. There is NOTHING recessionary on this board. The risk has flipped sides: it is now that the Fed is behind a re-accelerating inflation with an economy running above 3 pct, and that the next move priced is a HIKE rather than a cut. The three things that would break the picture are a confirmed hit on Saudi crude infrastructure, an ISM miss on Monday, and the midterms on Tuesday. WATCH, IN ORDER OF WEIGHT: ISM Monday as the first hard activity read after a 3.4 pct GDP print; whether T5YIFR keeps climbing from 2.27 now that core PCE is rising; the midterms Tuesday and any read-through to the Fed and to fiscal policy; OPEC+ Sunday; whether the dollar ever responds to hot US data; whether Riyadh confirms refinery damage; getting a live MOVE print; the Oct 28 H.4.1 landing in WALCL; rotating the embedded PAT; clearing the .git lock files.
